newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria hold scrap iron managers for $2 million graft.
newsitem.headline: Algeria hold scrap iron managers for $2 million graft.

text.p: The Algerian authorities, clamping down on corruption, have arrested three senior managers of the capital's local government scrap iron enterprise suspected of embezzling 110 million dinars ($2.0 million).

The official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday the chief executive, his deputy and the technical department head, appeared before a judge last week and were ordered to be held in custody pending trial.

They were charged with "economic sabotage, embezzlement" which caused the company about 110 million dinars loss, said APS. They were also accused of "significant questionable deals" with unspecifed foreign companies.
News of their arrests emerged one day after President Liamine Zeroual appointed former justice minister Hamdani Benkhelil to head a government watchdog to fight corruption.

Zeroual, who was returned to power following his victory in last year's presidential poll, promised voters to erase corruption seen as a main factor in a lack of trust between ordinary Algerians and their leaders.
